pill.desc: pale yellow, oval, biconvex, film-coated tablet

clues.kinetics: Plasma protein binding is 86.2%, and a high-fat meal lowers exposure by only about 16%, so food is not clinically relevant. Most of the dose is excreted in urine (54.4%) and feces (41.2%).
clues.substance: A free base rather than a salt, with a molecular weight of 450.91. A non-hygroscopic powder that is very slightly soluble in water.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as 10 mg and 25 mg tablets, taken once daily.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Contraindicated in hypersensitivity to the drug or its excipients, and angioedema has occurred.
clues.indication: Heart failure, to cut cardiovascular death and hospitalization; chronic kidney disease at risk of progression; cardiovascular death in type 2 diabetes with established heart disease; glycemic control from age 10.
clues.mechanism: Inhibits SGLT2, the main kidney transporter reabsorbing glucose, so urinary glucose excretion rises; it also reduces sodium reabsorption.

tell: An SGLT2 inhibitor whose first listed indication is reducing cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: peak plasma concentrations of empagliflozin were reached at 1.5 hours post-dose
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: The apparent terminal elimination half-life of empagliflozin was estimated to be 12.4 h
